children.text: A2. Generate equal superposition of four basis states
You are given $$$N$$$ qubits in the zero state $$$|0...0 \rangle$$$. You are also given four distinct bit vectors which describe four different basis states on $$$N$$$ qubits $$$|\psi_i \rangle$$$.
Your task is to generate a state which is an equal superposition of the given basis states:
You have to implement an operation which takes the following inputs:

a two-dimensional array of Boolean values $$$bits$$$ representing the basis states $$$|\psi_i \rangle$$$. $$$bits$$$ will have exactly 4 elements, each of $$$bits[i]$$$ describing the basis state $$$|\psi_i \rangle$$$. Each of $$$bits[i]$$$ will have $$$N$$$ elements, $$$bits[i][j]$$$ giving the state of qubit $$$j$$$ in the basis state $$$|\psi_i \rangle$$$. Bit values true and false corresponding to $$$|1 \rangle$$$ and $$$|0 \rangle$$$ states, respectively; for example, for $$$N = 2$$$ an array
will represent the basis state $$$|01\rangle$$$. Each pair of $$$bits[i]$$$ and $$$bits[j]$$$ will differ in at least one position for $$$i \neq j$$$.
The operation doesn't have an output; its "output" is the state in which it leaves the qubits.
